items.headline: UMG Inks Deal With ElevenLabs to Develop AI Music Remix Platform
items.excerpt: Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs have signed a licensing and joint product deal to build an AI platform where fans can co-create, remix and mash up tracks from artists who opt in. It is ElevenLabs' first major-label agreement, struck without prior litigation.

items.headline: ElevenLabs strikes first deal with a major label to launch AI-powered music platform and audio products
items.excerpt: MusicTech details the ElevenLabs-UMG partnership: a licensed music platform plus new AI audio products, kept separate from ElevenLabs' existing Music API and ElevenMusic app. Artists and songwriters choose whether to participate.

items.headline: UMG's ElevenLabs deal is latest move to AI remix experiences
items.excerpt: Music Ally reads the ElevenLabs tie-up as part of UMG's steady push toward licensed 'AI remix' fan experiences, following its Kobalt and Merlin agreements. The pattern points to walled-garden creation tools rather than open prompt-to-song generators.

items.headline: Suno has rebuilt its AI music models from scratch with licensed music
items.excerpt: Suno's V6 family was retrained on licensed catalogue with Warner Music, BMG and Believe, and ships alongside tools that let users create with and remix music from participating artists.

items.headline: Suno v6: The Next Generation of AI Music Arrives - Now With Warner Music and BMG's Blessing
items.excerpt: A hands-on look at what Suno v6's three new models and editing tools actually do for producers, from stem-level control to revision workflows, now that the training set is licensed.

items.headline: Suno unveils upgrade developed with “music industry partners”, while continuing to battle the music industry in court
items.excerpt: Suno launched v6 with Warner, BMG and Believe as partners even as it keeps fighting UMG and Sony in court. CMU untangles which rights the new models rest on and which remain contested.

items.headline: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.excerpt: A new class action claims Suno encoded musicians' identities into its model and exploited them by using artists' names in prompts - a publicity-rights argument that sidesteps copyright entirely.

items.headline: Suno steals Artist Identities, Jason Isbell wants to stop it
items.excerpt: Jason Isbell and David Lowery's class action opens a new front in the AI music war: not training data, but the exploitation of an artist's unique sonic identity and name as a prompt handle.

items.headline: AI Music Disputes Need More Than a Label: 5 Records All Artists Should Keep
items.excerpt: A practical checklist for creators working with AI tools: keep consent records, source files, version histories, revenue trails and any challenges to unauthorised use, because platform AI labels alone won't settle a dispute.

items.headline: Acon Digital Acoustica 8: AI-Enhanced Post-Production
items.excerpt: Acoustica 8 adds AI-powered restoration, immersive/surround support and a reworked interface, folding machine-learning repair directly into a mastering and post-production editor.

items.headline: Dreamtonics Instrument X Replaces Big Sample Libraries With Neural Acoustics
items.excerpt: Dreamtonics' Instrument X swaps multi-gigabyte sample playback for neural acoustic modelling, promising expressive virtual instruments that respond to performance rather than triggering recorded takes.

items.headline: Google brings AI music generation directly into the Gemini app with its new Lyria 3.5 model
items.excerpt: Lyria 3.5 is now available in the Gemini app and API, generating full-length tracks with verses, choruses and bridges in high-fidelity stereo. Google says it was trained only on licensed content.

items.headline: Audacity 4, free and open-source audio editor, arrives with a revamped UI
items.excerpt: Audacity reaches v4 with a reworked interface and usability overhaul, alongside a suite of locally-run AI plugins for stem separation and transcription built with Intel. CDM also weighs the Tenacity fork.

items.headline: Serato's latest update introduces open streaming and 'Lucid Beatgrids' that can adapt to BPM changes
items.excerpt: Serato 5.0's beta brings analysis that tracks tempo drift in real time, so beatgrids follow live BPM changes instead of assuming a fixed grid - a quiet upgrade to the DJ's core workflow.

items.headline: IFPI urges EU countries to fully implement AI Act's new rules
items.excerpt: At the launch of its 'Music in the EU' report, the IFPI pressed member states to enforce the AI Act's transparency rules - the training-data disclosures that would let musicians see whether their work fed a model.
